Subject: Request: cross-border variance declaration & escrow details

Marissa —

Thanks again for the SOC 2 package. As part of our procurement and legal review we need two items clarified before we can proceed to approval:

1) A short declaration describing any allowed cross-border deviations from a single-region hosting requirement (we support EU-only, but have exceptions for disaster recovery or specific operator tasks). Please confirm which data flows, if any, may transit non-EU networks and under what controls.

2) An escrow/peering fallback plan for private peering that covers: a) who holds the escrow (technical artifacts for failover and contactability), b) how KMS access is partitioned when peering changes, and c) an attested egress control checklist.

We don't need full CAIQ responses immediately — a short, signed attestation and the peering escrow checklist will suffice to unblock legal.

Can you share by COB Thursday (Aug 27)?

Appreciate it —
Lisa Park
Head of Security, Aurelia Health
--
Aurelia Health (security@aureliahealth.com)

Lisa —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can provide a concise declaration and the peering escrow checklist. High level answers below; we'll attach a short attestation and a technical appendix with topology and KMS mapping.

- Cross-border variance: Redwood's standard EU deployment keeps customer data and model request processing within EU zones for primary production. Exceptions are only for operational tasks (scheduled snapshot transfer to secure US long-term archive for backups with customer consent) and multi-region failover. Any cross-border transit is restricted to encrypted channels, logged, and limited to metadata or encrypted snapshots — customer data plane for inference stays within the customer-selected region unless explicit opt-in or legal requirement.

- Escrow/peering fallback: We propose a three-party escrow model (Redwood + Aurelia + independent escrow provider). Technical artifacts held in escrow: VPC peering runbooks, BGP peering configs (redacted where needed), TLS certificate fingerprints, signed key-wrapping policies, and a template emergency-activation playbook. KMS: short-lived wrapped keys + an HSM-backed signing key that can be escrowed under multi-party governance; we will provide KMS partitioning mapping per tenant.

I'll route a draft attestation and the technical appendix to you by Thursday COB. Looping in infra and security for specifics.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Irene —

Attached are the items for the technical appendix. Highlights below (short bullets for the customer doc):

- Cross-border flows: production inference dataplane and KV cache are pinned to the customer EU tenant. Deviations: automated encrypted snapshots to an isolated long-term US archive (explicit customer opt-in) and DR warm standby in APAC for customers who have multi-region DR agreements.
- KMS partitioning: each tenant in EU uses a tenant-scoped KMS key stored in HSMs with region-bound key-wrapping. We create short-lived wrapped keys for any cross-region service operations; the wrapping key never leaves the HSM. See attached kms_partition_mapping.xlsx for the simple table (tenant_id -> key_type -> HSM_region).
- Escrow artifacts: runbook (runbook.md), BGP partial configs (redacted), peering contact matrix, signed copy of emergency activation playbook. Recommend Cloud Escrow Services (partners@cloud-escrow.net) as the third-party holder — they support sealed-keystore escrow and multi-party retrieval workflow.
- Egress checklist: list of allowed destination prefixes, egress firewall rules, mandatory TLS pinning, and sample audit log snippet showing a cross-region snapshot transfer with timestamps and audit fields.

Irene — drafted attestation language here (first pass):

"Redwood Inference attests that customer production inference data for tenants opting to host in the EU remains within EU zones for normal operation. Cross-region transfers are limited to encrypted snapshots and DR activation, performed only under documented governance and, where required, explicit customer consent. Redwood maintains multi-party escrow procedures for peering and failover artifacts to ensure recoverability without unintended exposure."

I'll drop the topology SVG and the zip of redacted configs into the shared drive link Marissa listed.

-Karthik
